description: Cut the sorted list at exactly 10 rows and drop rows tied with the 10th.

b.request: For each district with at least one account, calculate its account count, its share of all accounts, and that share minus the average share across districts with at least one account; return the district ID and those three values for exactly the 10 districts with the largest differences, ordered from highest to lowest, excluding any additional districts tied with the 10th, without rounding
b.sql: WITH district_counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), district_shares AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, account_count * 1.0 / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS account_share, 1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER () AS average_share FROM district_counts) SELECT district_id, account_count, account_share, account_share - average_share AS share_difference FROM district_shares ORDER BY share_difference DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Sort by that difference from highest to lowest and return exactly 10 rows, dropping any other districts tied with the 10th. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH district_counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), shares AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, 1.0 * account_count / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS share FROM district_counts) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference_from_average_share FROM shares ORDER BY difference_from_average_share DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Which are the top 10 districts by that difference, from highest to lowest? Don't round anything. Cut the sorted list at exactly 10 rows and drop rows tied with the 10th.
c.sql: WITH district_counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), district_shares AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, 1.0 * account_count / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS share FROM district_counts), ranked AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS above_average_share FROM district_shares) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, above_average_share FROM ranked ORDER BY above_average_share DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), calculate its account count, its share of all accounts, and the difference between that share and the average share across districts. Return the district id and these three values for exactly the 10 districts with the highest differences, sorted from highest to lowest. Exclude any additional districts tied with the 10th row, and do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH district_counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), district_shares AS (SELECT district_id, account_count, 1.0 * account_count / SUM(account_count) OVER () AS account_share FROM district_counts) SELECT district_id, account_count, account_share, account_share - AVG(account_share) OVER () AS share_difference FROM district_shares ORDER BY share_difference DESC, district_id LIMIT 10
